verdict: The curve, whatever it is, recorded per the task's own rule: DECODE is faster on two cards in both boots (+85% and +41% paired); PREFILL scales strongly NEGATIVE (-3x at 2 cards, -5x at 4, deterministic in sign, both boots). The honest headline is that WITHIN-ARM BOOT VARIANCE (control decode 7.72 vs 6.07, 4-card decode 12.90 vs 5.86) is as large as the between-arm differences, so single-pair scaling numbers on this box are noise-shaped and the 4-card decode mean is NOT distinguishable from control.
session: TS 20261026-235443, six boots in ONE session, interleaved order (ctl, 2c, 4c, ctl, 2c, 4c) per the DSpark swap-repeat rule; runner tools/gfx906/run-p5.4-split-smoke.sh ARMS subset; parity re-witnessed in the same session: d_4 == d_4b == d_ctl 64/64 bitwise, guard PASS (74 passes, 222 hand-offs, 2.70 ms/pass warm)

expert_paths_per_run_stable_across_arms.staged_both_2_and_4: 14528 hit / 169 cpu / 423 pcie / 27 file (96.1% VRAM), cpu 33 ms, file 89 ms

findings: the expert tier is ONE card's (re-confirmed at 2-card: sampler peaks 27.13/5.75 GiB - owner holds tier+dense[0,20), stage 1 holds dense[20,40) only). The decode speed-up on two cards therefore comes ENTIRELY from spreading the DENSE compute (attention + dense FFN + rings) across cards, not from expert caching - that is task #39's prize, not this code's.

prefill's 4.3x file-tier read amplification under staging is the negative-scaling limiter, named: the staged prefill's per-stage tier queries cycle the shared VRAM slots worse (8875 vs 2073 file reads) and the file path is ~6 GB/s; the relay itself is NOT the limiter (2.70 ms/pass warm, 166 MiB total across 222 hand-offs).

boot-to-boot variance on this box exceeded arm separation for every metric; the within-arm spread is reported beside every mean and NO scaling claim stronger than 'two-card decode was faster in both paired boots' is made. n=2 per arm; a defensible curve needs n>=4 interleaved boots and would still be bounded by the same variance.

the serve round-trip the task asked for is REFUSED BY DESIGN: the staged engine rejects --serve (conversation snapshot/restore is per-instance; START-HERE refused-with-a-message list). Recorded as the boundary, not worked around.
glm: NOT measured: its staged parity is a known defect (task #40) and scaling numbers from an engine with a correctness defect must not enter a curve anyone quotes. #31 must close P5 with the GLM boundary named.
not_tested: GLM scaling (#40 first); n>=4 boots per arm; concurrent/serve traffic (refused); MTP x staged (refused pair); the cross-device slot-budget defect (staged reads its expert budget from the owner card's free VRAM - ~6 GiB under-used on 0,1 runs) was NOT fixed here, cited as a #39 precondition - fixing it may change every staged number in this file
